Thanks. To check which programmes fit, I need a few more details:
1. Does anyone live with you under 18? If so, how many children? (none; 1; 2; 3; 4 or more)
2. Roughly how much does the household earn from work in a year, before tax? (none; $1 to $10,000; $10,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $30,000; $30,000 to $40,000; $40,000 to $50,000; $50,000 to $60,000; $60,000 to $80,000; $80,000 to $100,000; $100,000 to $150,000; $150,000 or more)
3. Do you get any Social Security, pension, unemployment, child support, or other income? If so, roughly how much a year? (none; $1 to $5,000; $5,000 to $15,000; $15,000 or more)
4. Roughly how much is in your bank accounts and investments? (under $2,000; $2,000 to $5,000; $5,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $100,000; $100,000 or more)
5. Is anyone 65 or older, or does anyone have a disability? (no; yes)

summary: Household: Kansas, single parent, one child aged 3, renting, no other income, small savings (roughly $2k-5k), no one 65+, employer health insurance available. Work income and disability status could not be confirmed; the household said they would need to check. Recommended: SNAP (likely at low-to-moderate income), WIC (child under 5, income test), Medicaid and CHIP for the child (KanCare; child-only eligibility at these incomes), EITC and refundable CTC (need earned income; EITC phases out around $50k, CTC refund needs earnings above $2,500). Not recommended: ACA premium tax credit (employer insurance available), school meals (child not yet school-age), SSI (no disability reported; revisit if one is found), TANF (Kansas limits are strict; caseworker to check if income is very low). Hand off to a caseworker to verify exact earnings and disability status before applying.
